lines.text: Sam stood in front of the old calendar on the laundromat wall, and counted the days with his finger. Twice. Then he turned around and said it out loud. It's Thanksgiving. Oakhaven. Day twenty. Thanksgiving. Before sunrise, he sent the sharpshooters out to the woods west of town. Jaylozy brought down a deer. Caleb and Quinn each came home with a turkey. Everyone else stayed back and built two tables. Doors off their hinges. Planks from the woodpile. Every crate and bucket on the block, lined up in two rows, end to end across the yard. When the hunters got back, Victoria and Kathryn took over the cooking fire, and didn't let anyone near it for hours. Then everyone sat down. Forty-three of us, along two long tables. Old army MREs. Cans of soup. Vegetables from Mateen's garden. And fresh game, for the first time since this started. Somebody laughed, and nobody told them to be quiet. Nobody watched the fence. For the first time in weeks, everything felt normal. Happy Thanksgiving, from all of us in Oakhaven.
